messages:
mia: heads-up — since last night's rollout we're seeing a p99 bump on eventstream SSE endpoints (~+180ms). users hitting toolcall flows complain about slow tail latency. I rolled local traces and CI nightly flagged a perf regression at 1928720000. Anyone else seeing this?
perf-bot: nightly-perf: regression detected on branch main. p50 +12ms, p95 +48ms, p99 +180ms for /v1/eventstream. CI job: perf/integration/streams failed thresholds. link: https://ci.internal/perf/192872
rohan: looking now. flamegraph from a replay shows higher syscall time and extra JSON.stringify in the toolcall serialization path. also more context switches during frame flush. attaching quick flame: https://perf.gist/rohan/stream-flame
sylvia: I pulled metrics — KV cache hit rate dropped from 96% -> 71% for the same workload after the merge that normalized cache keys (PR 4387). miss rate aligns with increased serialize calls. histogram: keys per request shifted, lots of miss churn.
archie: I replayed traffic with and without the recent batching heuristic tweak (PR 4350). Heuristic now prefers smaller batches for latency-sensitive tags which forces a different kernel selection in the runtime. That increases kernel setup overhead ~40us per request; compounded at high QPS looks like your p99 bump.
mia: ok so potentially two interacting faults: cache-key normalization causing KV misses and batching heuristic causing suboptimal kernel choice, both increasing serialization/toolcall overhead in the SSE path. can we bisect to decide root cause?
rohan: quick experiment — I forced old batching config in staging and reran replay: p99 drops ~100ms but still above baseline. then I disabled the new key-normalizer and p99 returns to baseline. so key-normalizer looks primary.
sylvia: confirmed — when cache-key schema changed we started storing toolcall frames with extra metadata which increases serialized size, and the runtime's streaming serializer is sensitive to those header fields; extra bytes force slower code path.
archie: noted a secondary orthogonal effect: the kernel selector uses median sequence length to pick kernels; normalized keys increased avg seq length for some traces (more metadata in toolcall), so kernel choice shifted. that explains why changing batching alone helped some.
mia: we need a short plan: 1) revert key-normalizer (PR 4387) to stop regression 2) patch runtime serializer to avoid slow path for small header changes 3) add canary with old batching tuned to avoid kernel-shift for now. thoughts? :eyes:
rohan: opening revert PR for 4387 now and adding a follow-up to rework key normalization into a backward compatible form. I'll also include a perf test against the streaming toolcall pattern.
sylvia: I'll add a KV hit-rate alert and a synthetic test that asserts no sequence-length distribution shift after key changes. snippet for canary rule: ```yaml
route: /v1/eventstream
selector: header.x-customer-tier == "canary"
percent: 10
metrics: [p99_latency, kv_hit_rate]
```
perf-bot: canary rollout started for 10% traffic. baseline comparison scheduled.
deploy-bot: canary deployment: rollout/stream-canary-2026-03-18 started by rohan.
mia: after canary for 30m — p99 back to baseline on canary nodes, overall customer p99 improved ~140ms. Kernel selection metrics show reversion to previous kernel.
archie: bisect result: commit 9f3b2a1 (merge feature/key-normalizer) is the proximate cause; it changed key payload shape + introduced extra meta header. batching tweak exacerbated but wasn't root cause.
rohan: created PR 4399 to revert 9f3b2a1. Also adding a perf unit that replays toolcall-heavy SSE and asserts p99 < baseline+10ms.
sylvia: after revert we should add end-to-end test and a KV schema migration plan. I'll own the alerting work.
mia: decision: revert 9f3b2a1 (PR 4399) merged to main, follow-up PRs for serializer optimization and batching thresholds. owners: rohan (revert + tests), sylvia (KV alerts + migration), archie (kernel selector docs + tuning). I'll file the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
rohan: thanks — monitoring dashboards updated, keeping the canary running for 1h to be safe.
perf-bot: CI perf job for main now within thresholds after revert. p99 back to historical range.
mia: great work team, let's capture lessons for future key-shape changes (add perf checklist + synthetic replay). :thumbsup:
